Verdict: Not ready for registration. The 17-row universe/filter is defensible and appears complete, but the declared single-source plan does not ground the `Year of Accession` column. The artifacts themselves say those years come from per-country/per-monarch Wikipedia pages, while `source_urls` contains only `List_of_current_monarchies`. A directly relevant Wiki-family source, `List of current monarchs of sovereign states`, supplies the missing `Since` values but is not cited.

Findings:
1. `Year of Accession` is under-grounded by the declared `source_urls` / `source_count`.
   - Type/severity: structural, BLOCKING.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: `draft.json::source_count = 1` and `source_urls` contains only `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`. But `draft.json::temporal_note` says Year of Accession is per the per-country Wikipedia article, `_extraction_notes` says Year of Accession requires per-country cross-reference, and `curation.json::source_coverage_notes` says the year is only implicit in the master article's Monarch column. That is not enough for a registered answer-key column.
   - Evidence from staged ground-truth source: the cited master article's main table header is `Monarchy / Official local name(s) / Title of Head of State / Monarch / Title of Head of Government / Type of monarchy / Succession / Current constitution`; it has no accession-year or `Since` column (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`, lines 162-168). Example rows confirm the final numeric field is constitution year, not monarch accession year: Denmark lists Frederik X but ends with `1849`, not 2024 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`, lines 182-184); Sweden ends with `1974`, not Carl XVI Gustaf's accession year 1973 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`, lines 223-225); the UK row has `No codified constitution`, not 2022 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`, lines 230-233).
   - Evidence from validation/challenge Wiki-family source: `List of current monarchs of sovereign states` is linked from the cited source and directly supplies the missing accession dates in a `Since` column: Charles III / Commonwealth realms since 8 September 2022 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states`, lines 184-201); Denmark/Frederik X since 14 January 2024; Eswatini/Mswati III since 25 April 1986; Jordan/Abdullah II since 7 February 1999; Lesotho/Letsie III since 7 February 1996 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states`, lines 212-225); Saudi Arabia/Salman since 23 January 2015, Spain/Felipe VI since 19 June 2014, Sweden/Carl XVI Gustaf since 15 September 1973, Thailand/Vajiralongkorn since 13 October 2016, and Tonga/Tupou VI since 18 March 2012 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states`, lines 244-253). Per-monarch pages also support the spot-checked years: Frederik X reign begins 14 January 2024 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederik_X`, lines 206-208 and 323-325); Charles III reign begins 8 September 2022 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III`, lines 309-312 and 502-504); Carl XVI Gustaf reign begins 15 September 1973 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_XVI_Gustaf`, lines 228-230 and 316-319); Mswati III reign begins 25 April 1986 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mswati_III`, lines 193-195 and 313).
   - Impact: the row values are likely repairable, but the registered source metadata would be false as written. This is blocking because an entire non-key column depends on uncited sources.
   - Minimal repair: add `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states` to `source_urls`, update `source_count` to 2, and update `source_coverage_notes`, `temporal_note`, `_extraction_notes`, and `decision_log` so `List_of_current_monarchies` is the universe/type source and `List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states` is the monarch/accession-year value source. Alternatively add 17 per-monarch pages, but the single current-monarchs list is cleaner and already linked from the cited master article.

2. Thailand monarch-name provenance is internally inconsistent.
   - Type/severity: structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE.
   - Evidence from staged artifacts: CSV stages `Thailand,Asia,Parliamentary,Vajiralongkorn,2016`. `curation.json::normalization_decisions` says the master article gives Thailand's monarch as `Rama X` and that staged values match the master article's short-form. That is internally inconsistent.
   - Evidence from staged ground-truth source: `List_of_current_monarchies` displays Thailand's monarch as `Rama X` (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchies`, lines 223-225). The display link targets the `Vajiralongkorn` article, so the staged value identifies the same person, but it is not verbatim display text.
   - Evidence from validation source: `List of current monarchs of sovereign states` lists the Thai monarch as `Rama X, Vajiralongkorn`, which supports either display convention if that source is added (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_current_monarchs_of_sovereign_states`, lines 248-251).
   - Impact: not blocking because the entity is correct and a linked Wiki-family source supports the personal-name form. It should be documented as link-target/personal-name normalization, or the cell should be changed to `Rama X` if the curator wants strict display-text parity with `List_of_current_monarchies`.
